launch.description: Arguments of `launch` as the engine receives them. The extension resolves launch.json first: a `.dll` program becomes `program: <dotnet.exe of the chosen bitness>, args: [<dll>, ...]`, and a .NET Framework exe gets `__dotnetFramework`. launch.json properties that only the extension reads (`architecture`, `sourceFileMap`, `sourceSearchPaths`, `processName`, `waitTimeout`) are not listed here.

program.description: Full path of the exe to start (a .NET apphost, a .NET Framework exe, or dotnet.exe).

env.description: Environment variables added for the program. `null` removes a variable.

stopAtEntry.description: Stop at the first line of the user's `Main` (also for `async Main`).

justMyCode.description: Only modules with symbols, without `DebuggerNonUserCode` / `DebuggerHidden` / `DebuggerStepThrough`, are user code (default true).

enableStepFiltering.description: Step over property accessors and operators when stepping in (default true).

__dotnetFramework.description: Set by the extension when `program` is a .NET Framework exe: the engine starts it with the .NET Framework CLR (no .NET runtime needed).

attach.description: Arguments of `attach`. The process must have its runtime (coreclr.dll or clr.dll) loaded and be of the engine's bitness.

processId.description: Process id. A string is accepted too (`${command:pickProcess}` returns one).

messages.name: dotnetX86.freezeThread
messages.description: Freezes or thaws a thread: a frozen thread stays suspended across `continue`, steps and evaluations until thawed.

threadId.description: The thread (`threads`' id, the OS thread id).

messages.name: dotnetX86.handleStats
messages.description: For the types that hold a native handle in a field, counts the objects and those whose handle is not 0 (not disposed). The field may be declared by a base type (`Bitmap` holds `Image._nativeImage`).

fields.description: The fields to look at, by declaring type (`Namespace.Name`) and field name.

types.description: By type name; types without one of the fields are left out.

messages.name: dotnetX86.heapStats
messages.description: Counts the objects on the GC heap by type, while the program is stopped. Fails while a GC is in progress.

types.description: Largest total size first. Free space between objects is counted under the name `?`.

messages.name: dotnetX86.makeObjectId
messages.description: Gives the object a value refers to an id (`$1`) that stays valid while the program runs (a weak GC handle: it does not keep the object alive, and reads `null` once the object is collected). In expressions the extension writes `$1` as `__DOTNETX86_OBJID_1`; values of objects with an id end with ` {$1}`.

id.description: The new id (1, 2, ...); the same object asked twice keeps its first id.

messages.name: dotnetX86.pauseForFreeze
messages.description: Pauses the program because this UI thread stopped answering for `ms`; the stop is reported on that thread with the description "UI not responding for N s".

messages.name: dotnetX86.setEventTrace
messages.description: Traces the firing of event handlers without stopping (function breakpoints the relay continues from).

handlers.description: The handlers to trace (added to those already traced).

messages.name: dotnetX86.setExceptionTypes
messages.description: The exception types checked in the Exception Settings view changed: the relay stops on these when they are thrown.

messages.name: dotnetX86.mcpEndpoint
messages.description: Sent once after `initialize` when the engine was started with `--mcp-listen` (setting `dotnetX86.mcp.enabled`): where AI clients can control this session through MCP (Streamable HTTP, JSON answers only). The extension offers it to VS Code's AI as an HTTP MCP server. The engine also writes it to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\dotnet-x86dbg\mcp\<enginePid>.json` (removed on exit), where `dotnet-x86dbg --mcp-connect` finds it for AI clients outside VS Code.

url.description: `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp`. Requests from a web page (an `Origin` other than localhost or VS Code) are refused.

token.description: Required as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; made anew for every engine.

messages.name: output
messages.description: Standard DAP `output`. Categories: `stdout` / `stderr` (the program's output, decoded as UTF-8 while it is valid, else in the console code page), `console` (Debug.WriteLine and the engine's notes), `important` (an evaluation that had to run the other threads to finish).

messages.name: process
messages.description: Sent once the program is started or attached to (after the `configurationDone` response). The extension starts the memory graph and the UI freeze watch with `systemProcessId`.

name.description: The program's path (launch) or the process's exe (attach).

messages.name: stopped
messages.description: Standard DAP `stopped`. The engine sends `breakpoint` (also function breakpoints), `step`, `exception`, `pause` (also `Debugger.Break()`) and `entry`; the relay sends `goto`, `data breakpoint` (Break on Value Change) and `step`.

messages.name: dotnetX86.controlEvent
messages.description: A traced event handler ran (event trace).

messages.name: dotnetX86.exceptionThrown
messages.description: An exception was thrown (exception log): sent for every throw while the log is on, whether the program stops or not.

stopped.description: Whether the program stopped for it.

snapshot.description: Call stack and local variables at the throw (when exceptionLog.captureLocals is on).

messages.name: dotnetX86.removeBreakpoint
messages.description: A temporary (`#once`) breakpoint was hit: the extension removes it from VS Code's list.

messages.name: dotnetX86.sqlExecuted
messages.description: A statement read from a database command (SQL log), with its parameters and the frames that ran it.

method.description: The provider method that ran it (`System.Data.SqlClient.SqlCommand.ExecuteReader`).

messages.name: dotnetX86.trackedValues
messages.description: Values of a `#track:` logpoint hit, or the time of a `#timer-start:` / `#timer-end:` section.

ExpressionEvaluationOptions.description: The same option as the C# extension's debugger (vsdbg).

allowImplicitFuncEval.description: Run property getters and `ToString()` / `DebuggerDisplay` to show values (default true). When false, properties come with `presentationHint.lazy` and run only when expanded; explicit evaluations (watch, hover, console) still run code.

name.description: Type name as the Variables view shows it (`System.Collections.Generic.List<int>`).

standardRequests.notes: Answers with the capabilities below, then sends `initialized`. Reads `supportsInvalidatedEvent`.
Checks the program (exists, bitness of the engine, .NET Framework 4.x) and remembers it; starts it at `configurationDone`.
Checks the process (runtime loaded, bitness of the engine); attaches at `configurationDone`.
Starts or attaches, then sends `process`. The relay first sets the SQL log's function breakpoints.
`condition` is a C# expression evaluated in the stopped program. The relay keeps `hitCondition`, `logMessage` and the `#once` / `#after` / `#changed` / `#caller` conditions to itself.

`Type.Method`, `Method`, `Namespace.Type.Method` (all overloads). `anyCode: true` binds outside user code too (SQL log, event trace). The relay adds its own breakpoints and cuts the response back to VS Code's.
Filters `all` and `user-unhandled`; `filterOptions[].condition` is `A, B` or `!A, B` (type names).
`exceptionId` is `CLR/<type>`, `breakMode` `always` / `unhandled` / `userUnhandled`, `details` with `message`, `stackTrace`, `innerException`.
The OS thread id is the DAP thread id. Names are `Thread.Name`; else the process's first thread is `Main Thread` (listed first) and the others `<No name>`.
Every managed frame, named `Namespace.Type.Method()` with the real type arguments; `startFrame` / `levels` page them.
One scope, `Locals`. A step over a call puts `<Type.Method> returned` first.
See the value conventions. Children carry `evaluateName`. `Static members` and `Raw View` are nodes of their own.
C# expressions with the compiler's values and types (lambdas, LINQ, `await` waited synchronously, pointers). The relay rewrites `$N` object ids.
The value is a C# expression.
Assigns to any assignable expression.
Frozen threads stay suspended.
Steps over `await` to the same method's continuation.
With `targetId`, the relay steps into the chosen call (Step Into Specific).
From an async method, returns to the awaiting caller.
The calls on the line, in the order they run.
Stops every thread (reason `pause`).
The lines of the same method that can be the next statement.
The engine moves the instruction pointer; the relay sends the `stopped` (reason `goto`).
Break on Value Change, emulated with breakpoints on the lines that write the variable.
Cancels a running evaluation.
Ends the program; `exited` and `terminated` follow.
Ends a launched program, detaches from an attached one (`terminateDebuggee` overrides).

startup.name: --interpreter=vscode
startup.notes: DAP over stdin / stdout (the default; accepted for netcoredbg compatibility).

startup.name: --log=<file>
startup.notes: Writes the DAP traffic and the engine's own log, flushed per line (setting `dotnetX86.trace`).

startup.name: --mcp-listen
startup.notes: Also accepts MCP on 127.0.0.1 with a token, and sends `dotnetX86.mcpEndpoint` (setting `dotnetX86.mcp.enabled`). The tools drive this session; VS Code follows through the usual DAP events.

startup.name: --mcp-connect[=<enginePid>]
startup.notes: Not used by the extension: run by AI clients outside VS Code, a stdio MCP server that relays to the latest engine started with `--mcp-listen` (or the given one).

startup.name: NETCOREDBG_SYMBOL_DIRS
startup.notes: Environment variable: folders (separated by `;`) searched first for PDBs, by module MVID (decompiled and downloaded symbols).

valueConventions.rule: `{Namespace.Type}`, or the `DebuggerDisplay` text; `DateTime`, `TimeSpan`, `Guid` and the like as `{ToString()}`.
Strings as C# literals (`"a\"b"`); chars as the code and the literal (`120 'x'`).
`{int[3]}`; collections with a DebuggerDisplay show it (`Count = 3`).
A value with an id ends with ` {$N}`; in expressions `$N` is sent as `__DOTNETX86_OBJID_N`.
Member names (`Read, Write` for flags); unnamed values as the number in the underlying type (`-6`).
The pointed value, with the pointer type in `type` (`int*`); `null` for 0.
The result is the exception object (`{System.InvalidOperationException}`); errors fail the request with a message saying what to do.
`Expression has been evaluated and has no value` with type `void`.
